newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish car makers attack road authority standards.
newsitem.headline: Swedish car makers attack road authority standards.

text.p: Swedish car makers AB Volvo and Saab Auto on Monday voiced fears for the future of the nation's car industry after the Road Authority effectively banned their cars from its fleet.

Sweden's Road Authority, which is responsible for the nation's roads, decided last week that it would no longer use cars that consume over 8.6 litres of petrol per 100 kms for environmental reasons nor cars that did not weigh between 1,000-1,500 kilos for safety reasons.
This would eliminate all Saab's from its fleet and all but two types of Volvo.
The Road Authority also recommended that other government bodies follow its lead.
Saab's president Robert Hendry on Monday wrote to Prime Minister Goran Persson, protesting about the decision.
He said there had been no discussions with the car industry before the decision was taken even though the government and industry have negotiations planned.

"I hope that the Swedish government's policy is to work for an improved environment in a comprehensive way at the same time as the conditions for the industry improve and the number of jobs increases," Hendry wrote in the letter.
"If not, there is cause to worry about what kind of future our industry has in this country."
Volvo has also expressed fierce opposition to the Road Authority's decision that is to take effect from January 1, 1998.
"We would like to know how they have come to there conclusions (over the environment and safety)," company spokesman Ingmar Hesslefors told Reuters.
"It is simplifying both environmental and safety measures to such a degree that makes it stupid.
"It is also very negative for the Swedish car industry. You would never get the German road authority acting in such a way."
Hesslefors said the Swedish car industry was calling on the government to have one policy for all the various government bodies.
"We keep hearing different things from different areas," Hesslefors said.
